The sentence of a script block as text

Source: R/result-head.R
result_titles.Rd

The title, subtitle and caption a script block shows, as the plain text now on screen. For a block_result_output() method that needs them outside the head row: in a downloaded file, or for a caption drawn under a table.

Usage

result_titles(session, ui = TRUE)

Arguments

session

The block's session, as the method received it.

ui

TRUE for the sentence as on screen, FALSE for the sentence without the script's ui_* lines.

Value

A list with

  • title, subtitle and caption, each one string or NULL;

  • filters, the filter trail that {filters} prints, as a character vector (empty when the input carries none);

  • declared, a character vector with those of "title", "subtitle" and "caption" that the script has a line for;

  • templates, a list keyed by the names in declared, each the line's text as written, "" for a line that is switched off.

Details

A line the script declares is resolved with the current control values and the data tokens ({n}, {label(col)}). A line it does not declare is the title the method gave to result_head(). A line that is neither, or that the script switched off, is NULL.

The sentence can change without the block being evaluated again, for example when a control that only the title names is changed. So read it where it is used and do not keep a copy: inside a render function the call takes a reactive dependency and the output follows the sentence, inside the content function of a downloadHandler it gives the current text.

Lines for the app only

A script can carry #| ui_title:, #| ui_subtitle: and #| ui_caption: lines, which are meant for the app: a ui_title or ui_caption replaces the plain line on screen and a ui_subtitle is added to it. With ui = TRUE the result is the sentence as on screen. A download or a report passes ui = FALSE and gets the sentence built from the plain lines only. Both forms follow the controls.

What the script declares

declared names the lines the script has, also one it switched off with nothing after the colon. So for caption:

  • in declared and a string: the script's caption;

  • in declared and NULL: the script switched the caption off, or it resolved to nothing;

  • not in declared and a string: the title the method gave;

  • not in declared and NULL: there is none.

templates holds the declared lines as the script wrote them, before anything is filled in, for a rule that depends on the wording, such as a caption that is exactly {filters}.

See also

result_head()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
block_result_output.my_table <- function(result, block, session, ...) {
  session$output$csv <- shiny::downloadHandler(
    filename = "table.csv",
    content = function(file) {
      # without the lines the script wrote for the app only
      writeLines(c(result_titles(session, ui = FALSE)$title, ""), file)
      utils::write.table(result$data, file, append = TRUE, sep = ",")
    }
  )
  shiny::renderUI(draw_my_table(result))
}
} # }
